text: Lesson 25 got a control written correctly, reviewed, and merged as code. That tells you the control is written right — it tells you nothing about what happens when real users, real sign-ins, and real devices actually hit it. A Conditional Access policy that looks correct in a Terraform diff can still lock out a legitimate finance team signing in from an unmanaged laptop once a quarter. Testing before enforcing is how you find that out before it becomes a help-desk incident instead of a line in a code review.

Conditional Access policies support a report-only state in addition to On and Off. In report-only, the policy evaluates every sign-in exactly as it would if enforced, and logs what it would have done, without actually blocking or challenging anyone. You review those sign-in logs for days or weeks, specifically for real business accounts marked "would fail," before ever flipping the policy to On and letting it actually grant or deny access.

Microsoft Defender's Attack Surface Reduction rules offer the same idea with four real states: Not configured, Block, Audit, and Warn. Audit mode logs every instance where the rule would have blocked an action, with nothing actually stopped; Warn shows the user a warning they can click through. Running a new ASR rule in Audit mode for a week surfaces the legitimate macro-enabled spreadsheet or tool it would have broken, before you ever commit to Block.

Once audit or report-only data looks clean, the next step still isn't the whole organization. Scope the control first to a small, representative pilot group — a mix of departments and device types, not just IT — so if something was missed, it affects a handful of volunteers instead of every employee at once. That's simulate first, enforce second, carried one step further.

A clean pilot still doesn't guarantee a clean full rollout — the business can push back once a control actually goes live everywhere. Next: the change-management discipline that keeps a technically correct control from getting rolled back or quietly exempted into uselessness.
